exposure: mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis C viral (HCV) infection
outcome: Sustained virologic response (SVR) rates after antiviral therapy
Time from therapy initiation to viral negativity
cohort: Pediatric HCV infection cases (n=373) born between 1973 and 2021 in Japan, collected from 65 pediatric institutions between 2012 and 2022.
finding: Approximately 10% of Japanese children with HCV infection acquired through mother-to-child transmission achieved spontaneous clearance, while DAA therapy demonstrated superior efficacy and faster viral clearance compared to interferon-based therapy.
followup_time: Up to the time of the study in 2022
